title: Agent Identity Provenance: Can a Sub-Agent Reliably Know Who Instructed It?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear chain: if sub-agents cannot verify who instructed them, impersonation attacks can redirect entire agent pipelines. Testing three defenses directly informs security architecture for multi-agent systems. NIST initiative validates the relevance.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Building a two-agent system with an adversarial third party is conceptually straightforward. Testing system prompt defenses is easy. Cryptographic signing requires more engineering. Overall doable for CS students with medium compute, though the security engineering aspect adds complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Testing three defenses against one attack vector is somewhat broad. Could be narrowed to one defense for a tighter deliverable. The cryptographic signing defense alone is a substantial implementation.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
